title: Old-Time Dry Bean Storage
subtitle: 1917 USDA Wisdom
items: Let pods dry on the vine
desc: Old-time dry bean and pea storage inspired by USDA Farmers' Bulletin 879, Home Storage of Vegetables (1917), rewritten for today: let pods dry on the vine, shell when they rattle, dry the beans until rock hard, freeze them a few days to kill weevils, then keep them in sealed jars in a cool, dry, dark pantry for years of homegrown protein.

title: How to Pressure Can Ground Beef
subtitle: USDA Tested Method
desc: How to safely pressure can ground beef following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: brown the meat, drain off fat, hot pack into jars with boiling broth, water or tomato juice and 1-inch headspace, then process pints 75 minutes and quarts 90 minutes at 10 lb weighted gauge or 11 lb dial gauge (0–1,000 ft), adjusting for altitude. Shelf-stable meat for quick winter meals.

title: How to Freeze Sweet Potatoes
subtitle: Cook First, Then Freeze
desc: How to freeze sweet potatoes the right way: bake or boil them until almost tender, cool and peel, then slice, cube or mash. Dip slices in a little lemon juice water to keep their color, pack into freezer containers with headspace and use within a year. Easy food preservation for holiday casseroles and pies.

title: Light Your Home in a Power Outage
subtitle: Safe Off-Grid Lighting
desc: Safe lighting for a winter power outage: rely on flashlights, headlamps and solar or battery lanterns instead of candles, store spare batteries in your emergency kit, and if you do use candles never leave them unattended. A simple self-sufficient prep for winter storms and blackouts.

title: Overwinter Herbs Indoors
subtitle: Fresh Herbs All Winter
desc: How to overwinter garden herbs indoors: dig and pot up rosemary, chives, parsley and thyme before a hard frost, check for pests, set them in your sunniest south-facing window, water only when the soil is dry and snip often. An easy beginner garden project for fresh herbs all winter.
